title: Path scrub misses absolute paths after '@', '**', '_', '>', '|', '#', ';', em dash, fullwidth colon, or Hangul (Claude Code @file mentions leak in prompt, title, say, ask, plan, summary)

const CONT = String.raw`(?:[ \t]+[^\s"'\`)\]}>,;\\/]+[\\/]${PCH}*)*`;
const ABS_PATH_RE = new RegExp(String.raw`(^|[\s"'\`(=:,[{<])((?:~|\.{1,2})?\/${PCH}+${CONT}|[A-Za-z]:\\${PCH}+${CONT})`, 'g');

title: Scheme-less URLs (github.com/org/repo/..., localhost:3000/..., 10.0.0.5:8080/...) keep their path and query
scenario: Text says 'see github.com/org/XUPATH?k=1', 'www.example.com/SECRETPATH?token=SECRETQ' or 'localhost:3000/SECRETPATH?x=SECRETQ' with no scheme.
actual: URL_IN_TEXT_RE requires 'scheme://'. ABS_PATH_RE does not fire because a letter or digit comes right before '/'. Path and query are sent unchanged. The scp form 'git@github.com:org/SECRETREPO.git' becomes '(email):org/SECRETREPO.git'. The e2e harness found XUPATHns markers in prompt, say, thinking, ask question/options, tool summaries, plan items, tool_end.error and system.text.
expected: Contract section 5: full URLs become host only, e.g. 'github.com'.

title: POST /config over 4096 bytes resets the connection instead of returning 413
scenario: A client POSTs a JSON body larger than MAX_BODY (4096 bytes) to /config with a valid Host header.
actual: readBody rejects and then calls req.destroy() synchronously. That tears down the socket before postConfig can write the 413 JSON, so the client sees ECONNRESET or EPIPE and never gets a status. Not exploitable, but the error path promised in the code (the 'body too large' branch) is dead.
expected: HTTP 413 {"error":"body too large"} with Connection: close, then the socket closes.
fix: On overflow, stop collecting (req.removeAllListeners('data'); req.resume() or req.pause()) and reject. In postConfig, send 413 with {connection:'close'} and destroy the socket on res 'finish'. Also check content-length up front and reject before reading.
verdictFix:
I tested this fix in $TMPDIR/co-skeptic/varB.mjs and varC.mjs.

1) In readBody, when the body goes over the limit:
   - set a `done` flag so later chunks are ignored, or remove the data listener;
   - do NOT call req.destroy();
   - reject with status 413.

2) In postConfig, handle 413 on its own path:
   - send(res, 413, JSON.stringify({error:'body too large'}), 'application/json; charset=utf-8', {'cache-control':'no-store', connection:'close'});
   - if needed, destroy the socket after res 'finish'.

3) Before reading, check Content-Length: if Number(req.headers['content-length']) > MAX_BODY, reply 413 right away with connection: close.

Results: varB (steps 1 and 2) and varC (steps 1 to 3) both return a clean 413 at 4097 B and 70000 B in every mode (Content-Length, chunked, slow writes, raw socket). varC also returns 413 for most 1 MB requests.

Two caveats:
- For very large bodies (1 MB to 20 MB) that the client sends all at once, closing the socket while unread data is still queued makes the kernel send a TCP reset, so the client may still see EPIPE or ECONNRESET. To make 413 reliable there, keep reading and discarding the rest of the body for a bounded amount of time or bytes (for example up to 64 KiB or 1 s) after sending 413, then destroy. Removing destroy with no limit at all (varA) gave the most reliable 413s, but it reads an unlimited body, so keep a limit.
- Calling req.pause() without draining causes earlier resets at 1 MB and above, because the socket closes with unread data.

title: Loopback-only bind is not per-user: any local process or other OS user can read /events and /state and POST /config without a credential
scenario: Shared macOS/Linux host, or any local untrusted process (a dev server, a malicious npm postinstall, another account). It connects to 127.0.0.1:4317 and sends Host: 127.0.0.1:4317 with no Origin.
actual: hostAllowed checks only the Host and Origin headers, and there is no token. Any loopback client gets the full snapshot: project keys (full cwd paths including the OS username), titles, prompts (up to 80 chars), say/thinking text and open questions. It can also change the poll interval.
expected: Optionally require a random per-run token printed in the URL (as Jupyter does) and passed back by the page (cookie or query on /events), or document clearly that loopback exposure is accepted.
fix: Generate a crypto.randomBytes(16) token at start. Print url?t=<token>. Have the page exchange it for an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, and require that cookie on /events, /state, /config and /healthz. Keep the Host and Origin checks.
verdictFix:
Scope the fix to the real threat: other OS users, and sandboxed processes that can reach the network but cannot read files. Same-user processes can read the 0600 transcripts directly, so do not claim the token protects against them.

Option A, documentation only (cheapest): change CONTRACT.md section 0 and the README 개인정보 section from "serves only to the local browser" to "any local process or OS user on this host can read the summaries (full project cwd, titles, 80-char prompt/say/thinking text)". Do this if multi-user hosts are out of scope.

Option B, per-run token. This keeps public/ untouched, which the contract assigns to the main session:
1. In start(), generate `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')`. Never pass it through argv or env (`ps` shows argv to other users). Return it as `{ url, token }`, and have bin print `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?t=<token>`.
2. Handle GET /?t=<token>:
   - Compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual, after checking that the lengths match.
   - On a match, reply 302 to `/` with `Set-Cookie: co_<port>=<token>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`. The redirect strips the token from the address bar and history.
   - On a wrong or missing token with no cookie, reply 403 with a short "open the URL printed by claude-office" message.
3. Require the cookie on /, /events, /state, and GET and POST /config. /js/*.js has no secrets and may stay open. /healthz only returns counts, so leaving it open is optional.
4. EventSource('/events') and fetch('/config') in public/js/sources.js are same-origin, so they send the cookie automatically. No page change

If that throws once, the error escapes to tick() and f stays {ready:false, needsAttach:false}. rescanOnce skips it forever ('if (f && !f.needsAttach) continue', line 149), and pollAll and idleAll skip it because !ready. The same throw also aborts the rest of that rescan, so later files and retryMeta/relinkAll are skipped for the tick.
actual: With one injected transient throw from the main's sessionEvent while a new sub attaches: after about 10 rescans and a live append, the page got 0 frames for the sub. It was not in the snapshot, while /healthz files=2 and store.has(sub)=true. A single log line: 'rescan loop failed: transient injected failure'. A separate run (exp6, throw in snapshotEvents during announce) recovered, because f.ready is set before announce, but only 1 of 3 sessions attached in that rescan.
expected: A failed attach is rolled back (files.delete plus store.detachFile) or marked needsAttach so the next rescan retries it. The rest of the rescan continues.
fix: Wrap the body of attach() after files.set in try/catch. On error, log it, run files.delete(ref.path), tailer.forget and store.detachFile, then return so the next rescan retries. Also wrap each attach call in rescanOnce so one bad file cannot skip the remaining attaches and retryMeta.
verdictFix:
I confirmed both changes below on throwaway copies under $TMPDIR/co-skeptic/patched and patched2. Each copy still passes the full suite (292/292), and in each the fault-mode repro recovers sub A ([session, say:live line from A], present in /state).

1. Main fix: roll back inside Runner.attach(). Wrap `this.store.attachFile(ref, state, { meta, label })` in try/catch. On error:
   - log `attach failed for <basename>`
   - `if (this.files.get(ref.path) === f) this.files.delete(ref.path)`
   - `this.tailer.forget(ref.path)`
   - `this.store.detachFile(ref.path)` (removes the half-registered byPath/byChar entry)
   - `return`
   Because the files entry is deleted, the next rescan sees no f and retries the attach. Do NOT ship only an outer try/catch in rescanOnce. It would swallow the throw but leave f in files as {ready:false, needsAttach:false}, which is exactly the zombie. An alternative to deleting: set `f.needsAttach = true` in the catch. rescanOnce would then re-attach it next tick, and attachFile drops the stale store entry through its prev lookup.

2. Also wrap `await this.attach(ref)` in a per-file try/catch inside rescanOnce. This keeps later refs, retryMeta() and relinkAll() running in the same tick. It also covers store.announce() -> entryEvents -> snapshotEvents and patch -> mainEvent, which run after f.ready=true and are outside any try today.

3. Optional extra safety (patched2): in Store.syncInfo, move `const parentProject = this.mainEvent(e.sid)?.project` inside the existing try that already guards setInfo. On its own this closes only this one callee; announce, r

title: POST /config re-arms the poll timer on every call, even with an unchanged value: repeated posts starve polling
scenario: setInterval(ms) calls every('poll', ms, ...), which does clearInterval plus a new setInterval each time. The UI control is <input type=number> and posts on 'change'. Holding a spinner arrow auto-repeats changes, and another local client could post in a loop.
actual: With intervalMs 250 and a POST every 100 ms (same value), there were 0 polls in 2 s, against 7 polls in 2 s without posts.
expected: Polling continues while the config is updated. An unchanged value is a no-op.
fix: Return early when ms === opts.intervalMs. Otherwise schedule the next poll relative to the last tick (a setTimeout chain that reads opts.intervalMs each time) instead of clearing and re-arming the interval.
verdictFix:
The fix needs both parts. The unchanged-value early return alone is not enough, because the realistic UI trigger (holding ArrowUp/Down or the spinner) sends a different value on every step, and that case still starves polling (0 polls in 2 s in my run).

1. In Runner.setInterval: if (ms === this.opts.intervalMs) return. postConfig can still broadcast.

2. A changed value must not push the next poll out. Pick one:
   (a) Turn poll into a self-rescheduling setTimeout chain. Roughly: const loop = () => { if (this.closed) return; this.timers.poll = setTimeout(() => { this.tick('poll', () => this.pollAll()).finally(loop); }, this.opts.intervalMs); this.timers.poll.unref?.(); }. setInterval(ms) then only assigns opts.intervalMs and never touches the timer. The new value takes effect at the next tick, and a running tick is never skipped.
   (b) Keep the setInterval loop but record lastPollStart in tick('poll'). On a change, arm a one-shot setTimeout for max(0, lastPollStart + ms - Date.now()) that runs a tick and then starts setInterval(ms).

close() already clears every timer with clearInterval, which also clears setTimeout handles in Node. Option (a) also needs the this.closed check shown above.

Regression test for test/server.test.mjs: use a counting Tailer (like the NullTailer fake, but poll increments a counter) and start with intervalMs 100. POST the same value every 30 ms for 600 ms and assert at least 3 polls. Then POST stepping values (150, 200, ...) every 30 ms and assert polls keep happening. Both assertions fail on the current code.

title: An unreadable attached transcript logs 'poll failed' on every tick with no backoff
scenario: An attached file becomes unreadable (EACCES; EIO is similar), while its stat still works and shows growth. pollAll catches the error and logs on every interval, and rescan re-tries attach for files that were never readable, logging each time.
actual: In 6.5 s at intervalMs 250: 25 'poll failed' lines and 3 'attach failed' lines. That is 4 lines/s indefinitely, or 20/s at 50 ms. The bin writes them all to stderr.
expected: Rate-limited or once-per-state-change logging, with backoff for a file that keeps failing.
fix: Keep a per-file error count and timestamp: log the first failure and then at most once per minute, and skip polling a failing file with exponential backoff. applyErrors already caps at 20; use the same idea here.
verdictFix:
File: src/server.mjs, Runner.pollAll (catch at line 247) and Runner.attach (catch at line 211).

1. Back off per file in pollAll; do not use a global counter.
   - Add pollErrors: 0, nextPollAt: 0 and lastErrCode: null to each `f` record.
   - In the filter, skip `f` while Date.now() < f.nextPollAt.
   - In the catch, log only when f.pollErrors === 0 or err.code !== f.lastErrCode. Then increment pollErrors and set nextPollAt = now + Math.min(intervalMs * 2 ** pollErrors, 30_000).
   - Keep the backoff capped (around 30 s, or rescanMs * 10) so a file that becomes readable again is picked up promptly.
   - On any successful poll, reset pollErrors, nextPollAt and lastErrCode. Optionally log "poll recovered for <basename>" once, so a later recover-then-fail cycle logs again.
   - Keep the current `continue`. Do not set needsAttach on EACCES or EIO: that would send the file through attach, causing attachFile/detachFile churn and re-announcing the session to open pages. Tailer state is kept on a throw, and resuming from the committed offset already works (verified).

2. Attach path, for files that were never readable. Keep a Map in Runner from path to the last error code (or to code plus ino and mtimeMs). Log only on the first failure for that path or when the code changes. Clear the entry when attach succeeds or when the path leaves scan(). rescanMs already limits the retry rate, so backoff here is optional. If you add it, retry early whenever ref.mtimeMs, ref.size or ref.ino changes.

3. At both sites, log err.code (falling back to errText) instead of the full message. Node's E

title: Oversized POST /config gets a connection reset instead of the intended 413
scenario: POST /config with a body over MAX_BODY (4096). readBody rejects and then immediately calls req.destroy(), which destroys the shared socket before postConfig can send its 413 JSON.
actual: Bodies of 5,000 and 100,000 bytes give the client ECONNRESET. A raw socket gets no status line at all. A 4,000-byte body gets 200.
expected: HTTP 413 {error:'body too large'}, then close the connection.
fix: On overflow, stop collecting (req.removeAllListeners('data'), req.resume()) and reject. Have postConfig send the 413 with 'connection: close' and let res.end close the socket; do not call req.destroy() before responding.
verdictFix:
In /Users/wahyzdad/coding/claude-office/src/server-http.mjs:

1. In readBody, keep a reference to the data handler. On overflow, do `req.off('data', onData); req.resume(); reject(Object.assign(new Error('body too large'), { status: 413 }));`. Drop `req.destroy()`. The late 'end' event calls resolve on an already-settled promise, which is harmless.

2. Add a cheap early reject in postConfig before reading anything: if `Number(req.headers['content-length']) > MAX_BODY`, call `req.resume()` and send 413 right away.

3. Decide the close policy deliberately. The suggested 'connection: close' only works for small overflows: in testing, a 1 MB body got the 413 and then EPIPE, and a 10 MB body got a TCP RST with the response lost. Two options:
   - (a) Recommended. Do not set 'connection: close'. Let req.resume() drain the rest and let Node reuse the connection. Every size tested up to 10 MB got its 413. Draining discards data without buffering it, and Node 20's default requestTimeout already limits how long that can take.
   - (b) If an unbounded drain is unacceptable, count drained bytes and only call req.destroy() after a second, larger cap (for example 1 MB) or after a short timer. That keeps the 413 for ordinary oversize bodies.

4. Optionally note the 413 behaviour in docs/CONTRACT.md next to "400 otherwise". Add a test to test/server.test.mjs that POSTs about 5000 bytes and asserts `status === 413` and `body.error === 'body too large'`. With the current code that test fails with ECONNRESET, which locks in the regression.

title: Replayed record timestamps ahead of the local clock freeze idle timers for the size of the skew
scenario: _touch uses the record timestamp for growth in replay and Date.now() when live, and only ever raises _lastGrowthMs. If replayed records carry timestamps ahead of the local clock (for example the clock was stepped back after they were written), idle(now) computes a negative 'quiet'. Held-rejection flush, the main end_turn fallback and sub done/idle ends then never fire until the wall clock catches up.
actual: A sub whose final text was replayed with timestamps 10 min ahead gets no idle events within 5 min. With no skew, session_end:done arrives at +16 s.
expected: Idle timing measured from when the server last saw growth, or with replayed timestamps clamped to now.
fix: In replay, clamp g to Math.min(Date.parse(ts), this._now()). Alternatively, track live growth in a separate monotonic field (performance.now-based) and use it for idle().
verdictFix:
Recommended fix: re-base inside idle() rather than clamping in _touch. It is one line, placed before the quiet computation at src/session.mjs:96:
  if (this._lastGrowthMs > nowMs) this._lastGrowthMs = nowMs;

This covers both causes of future-dated growth:
- (a) replayed timestamps ahead of the local clock
- (b) a wall-clock step back while records arrive live, which the suggested Math.min clamp in _touch does not handle

After the step, each timer waits exactly its normal threshold. The server calls idle() every second for every ready session, so the re-base happens about a second after attach.

Verified on a throwaway copy: 292/292 tests pass, and every skew scenario fires at the normal threshold.

If you prefer the _touch clamp (g = replay ? Math.min(Date.parse(c.ts ?? ''), this._now()) : this._now()), it also passes 292/292. It only fixes the replay case.

Optional regression test: replay a sub file whose final text has timestamps 10 minutes ahead of the injected clock, then assert that idle(clock.t + 15_000) returns session_end:done. Add a main-file twin for end_turn at +20 s.

A monotonic clock (performance.now) is not needed. idle() is given wall time by server.mjs:259, and the re-base already makes the delay independent of the size of the skew.
